Americas.headline: Colombia — 7.4-Magnitude Earthquake Kills Over 100
Americas.body: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia near San Jose del Palmar in the Chocó region, killing more than 100 people and damaging thousands of buildings. The epicenter was located roughly 400 kilometers west of Bogotá, with tremors felt across Ecuador, Venezuela, and Panama. Rescue teams are searching for survivors under collapsed structures, while international aid has begun arriving to support emergency operations.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Armed Gang Attack Leaves 47 Dead and Over 50 Kidnapped
Americas.body: Armed men launched an attack in Kenscoff, on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, killing at least 47 people, including five children, and kidnapping more than 50 others. The United Nations confirmed the casualties in what represents one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years. A gang leader publicly threatened to kill the hostages if Haitian National Police attempt a rescue operation.

Americas.headline: Colombia & Argentina — Severe Floods Displace Over 158,000
Americas.body: Simultaneous severe weather systems have triggered widespread flooding in Colombia and Argentina, affecting or displacing more than 158,000 people. In northern Colombia, record rainfall killed at least 14 people and affected 156,000 others, submerging roughly 80 percent of Córdoba department while destroying homes and crops. Meteorologists warn that flood conditions across both countries are expected to worsen through November.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Salvadoran Forces Launch Large Ground Offensive Against Gangs
Americas.body: Salvadoran military units launched their first major ground operation in Haiti, deploying armored vehicles into Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and killing at least 12 fighters from the 400 Mawozo and Chèn Méchan gangs. The offensive follows the October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran technicians serving with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force. El Salvador currently maintains over 2,000 military personnel in Haiti under an authorized deployment through October 2027.

Africa.headline: Why an Ebola outbreak in Africa doesn’t mean an epidemic in Britain
Africa.body: Parts of Africa are facing the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic on record. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, one of several types of Ebola virus, and has grown dramatically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Cases have now appeared in other countries too. By October 31, 2026, the DRC had recorded 10,467 cases and 5,103 deaths. Kenya and Nigeria have also reported cases, and Uganda was affected earlier in the outbreak. Conflict and an ongoing humanitarian crisis make it harder for health workers to find cases, treat patients and track those who have been exposed. Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian strike on humanitarian aid hub in Zaporizhzhia region
Europe.body: A Russian strike targeted a humanitarian aid center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, causing extensive casualties among civilians gathered for assistance. Ukrainian officials confirmed dozens of people were killed or remain missing following the bombardment. According to local reporting, the confirmed death toll has risen to at least 31 people. The facility was actively providing relief supplies when it was struck, making it one of the deadliest single attacks on humanitarian infrastructure during the war.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Massive power grid strikes and acute front-line food insecurity
Europe.body: Russian forces launched one of the war's largest coordinated attacks against Ukraine's national power grid, causing widespread electrical outages and threatening vital municipal services. Concurrently, civilian hardship remains acute near front-line areas. In Zaporizhzhia, an estimated 2,000 civilians—including unaccompanied children—gathered at a single cathedral to receive emergency food rations as daily Russian drone and artillery strikes continued across the city.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Escalating attacks disrupt education across two-thirds of school days
Europe.body: Air-raid alarms are now disrupting nearly two-thirds of school days across Ukraine, severely impeding children's access to safe education. Frequent alarms force students and teachers into shelters, compounding psychological trauma and learning loss. In response, UNICEF is partnering with the Ukrainian government to reinforce school bomb shelters, offer mental health support, and deliver catch-up learning programs to maintain educational continuity for vulnerable children.

Europe.headline: Russia — Hantavirus outbreak infects over 1,500 people across multiple regions
Europe.body: Health authorities in Russia report an outbreak of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by hantavirus, with 1,512 patients diagnosed across several regions. Official figures record 656 cases in Udmurtia, 367 in Bashkortostan, and 278 in the Nizhny Novgorod Region, along with additional infections in Tatarstan and Saratov. The surge is linked to seasonal autumn migrations of wild rodents into human habitats, exposing residents to infected droppings and saliva.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DR Congo — Over 5,000 dead in rapidly spreading Ebola epidemic
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing a severe Ebola epidemic caused by the Bundibugyo virus, recording 10,467 cases and 5,103 deaths as of 31 October 2026. Cases have also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria, following earlier infections in Uganda. Ongoing armed conflict and humanitarian distress in affected regions are heavily impeding health personnel from tracking contacts and delivering medical treatment. In response to regional risks, UNICEF has delivered over 50 metric tonnes of personal protective equipment and infection control materials to assist preparedness efforts in neighbouring South Sudan.
verified_figures: over 50 metric tonnes of supplies delivered to South Sudan

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: South Sudan — 42 new cholera cases reported in Unity State
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Health officials in South Sudan's Unity State reported 42 new cholera cases within a 24-hour period, primarily concentrated in Rubkona County and the state capital of Bentiu. Despite the newly registered infections, health authorities noted that the overall rate of transmission has decreased over the past two months compared to earlier stages of the outbreak.
